maradi-central-market-works-before-compe.drop_reason: Niger, Local Urban Infrastructure Development Project. Cut on the check, not by the writer. Checked in the outcome document: the whole of the harm is one sentence in paragraph 35 of the completion report of 1 July 2013 — "The project was generally implemented in compliance with safeguards policies, but in several cases did works start with sites still occupied by affected persons, or compensation of affected persons was not assured before commencement of works." Read whole, that sentence does not say how many cases there were, does not say where any of them was, and is disjunctive about what happened in them: either works began on an occupied site or compensation was not assured. The same paragraph closes the matter: "At the time of finalizing this ICR, all issues raised during project implementation support missions and in technical audit reports have been fully resolved and proof of adequate compensation of all project affected persons has been provided to the World Bank." The only other people-bearing figures in the report are 2,712 persons affected and 2,586 traders "affected by the temporary and voluntary relocation" of the Marché Central — a count of people affected, and a relocation the report calls voluntary. Paragraph 59 records that people in Niamey Commune V "had already voluntarily relocated temporarily" for road works the project then dropped; no count, and no works. The only version of the finding that carries a count and a site — three persons who had given only tacit agreement before work started on two public latrines and one water kiosk — exists solely as a clarification the project team and the task team leader gave the Evaluation Group during its review (ICR Review of 14 October 2014, sections 8 and 11a: "The project team has since provided further clarification. According to the TTL..."), and a number staff gave the Bank's evaluators during a review is not a document. Against the standing limb (b) edge, which has compensation unpaid in five identified resettlement cases at a named site, this has no count, no site, and nothing outstanding. Limb (a) fails for want of any count of people relocated. ICIJ gives 148. Recorded separately in the check log: the review prints, inside quotation marks and attributed to the completion report, a sentence the completion report does not contain.

nouakchott-rosso-corridor-temporary-move.drop_reason: Mauritania Road Corridor Project. Cut on the check, not by the writer, who named it their weakest entry and invited the test. Two independent grounds. First, the figure. The completion report of 8 October 2015 states its 250 twice and not in the same terms. Annex 2, Outputs by Component, says the consultant "worked with the Government to compensate the 250 persons who had to temporarily move their homes or businesses due to the construction works as part of the ARAP". Paragraph 27, the safeguards narrative and the document's own account of what happened, says the consultant and the hired non-governmental organisation "interviewed some 250 persons who were temporarily displaced or affected by the road works, and subsequently compensated these persons". The Evaluation Group's review lists the output as "250 people satisfactorily relocated and/or compensated" and elsewhere as people "displaced or affected by the road works and subsequently resettled". Two of the three statements of the figure are disjunctive, and `displaced` holds only a count of people relocated, never "affected": where a document's narrative cannot say whether its 250 were moved or only affected, a single cell in a deliverables table cannot certify the count. Round 19 cut a figure on exactly this shape, "compensated and/or resettled". With the figure in the note rather than the field there is no count, so limb (a) fails, and limb (b) fails too: the move was temporary and both documents record the compensation as settled in full — the grantee's annex says "persons affected by the project were consulted and compensated at the rate of 32,431,905 MRO and claims were handled without reservation as confirmed by the absence of complaints", and the report adds that "All persons affected by the project were properly consulted and compensated and all claims settled without reservation" and that no work accidents occurred. A move with no loss recorded on top of it is not harm. Second, the lender link. The grant and the government co-financed Lot 2 only, the 47 km Bombri to Rosso section; the European Union financed Lot 1, the 145 km Nouakchott to Bombri section, which was still under construction at closing. No document says how many of the 250 were on the 47 km the grant paid for. The report further records that the environmental and social assessment and management plan were "financed from the TSIDTAP", a different operation, and that "the Government was efficient in implementing and funding the ESMP and ARAP" — the compensation was paid by the government, not from the grant. ICIJ gives 110. Not a plan reprint: the 250 appears in no plan or appraisal document, and the appraisal document's only 250 is a line item of US$250,000 for technical audit.

sao-gabriel-cable-station-urban-farmers.title: Seven farmers lose land and income to the São Gabriel cable station works
sao-gabriel-cable-station-urban-farmers.place: São Gabriel, Água Grande district, São Tomé Island, São Tomé and Príncipe
sao-gabriel-cable-station-urban-farmers.point: São Gabriel, from Nominatim. The assessment report names São Gabriel as the site of the cable station but gives no address for the parking and fuel area that took the farmed land.

lenders.name: World Bank (International Development Association)
lenders.role: Project P117652, Central African Backbone Program second phase (CAB2). IDA Grant H6420, SDR 9.8 million, about US$14.9 million equivalent, fully disbursed. Approved 20 January 2011, closed 31 December 2014 (completion report ICR00003141, 17 June 2015). Environmental category B. Two safeguard policies were triggered: Environmental Assessment (OP/BP 4.01) and Involuntary Resettlement (OP/BP 4.12). The completion report rates the outcome Highly Satisfactory, risk to development outcome Low or Negligible, and Bank and borrower performance Satisfactory. The Evaluation Group's review of 23 October 2015 also rates the outcome Highly Satisfactory, and prints the completion report's risk rating as Negligible to Low. The Group's field-based assessment report of 4 June 2018 rates the outcome Satisfactory.

companies.name: Companhia Santomense de Telecomunicações (CST)
companies.role: The national telecommunications operator. It owned the building chosen for the cable station and the land being farmed beside it, and paid all the compensation under the Abbreviated Resettlement Action Plan.

companies.name: Agência Fiduciária de Administração de Projecto (AFAP)
companies.role: The government's fiduciary agency for donor-funded projects; it handled the project's procurement and financial management.

sao-gabriel-cable-station-urban-farmers.community: The grant paid for São Tomé and Príncipe to join the ACE submarine cable and for a cable landing station. The Evaluation Group's field-based assessment report says the operator chose one of its existing buildings at São Gabriel for the station, and that the parking and fuel infrastructure beside the building needed land that was being used for urban farming. The land was owned by the operator and not by the farmers. The Abbreviated Resettlement Action Plan of 4 July 2011 counts seven: "There are seven farmers that will be impacted upon and will loose a portion of the land they cultivate", and its Appendix 1 opens "The following seven PAPs will be affected" and carries a data sheet for each, with age, schooling and household. Most of the seven said they had farmed the garden for about fifteen years and sold the produce at the market; the crops were cabbage, onions, green peppers and sweet potatoes. One was expected to lose about 70 per cent of the land he cultivated and another about half; one, a medical specialist, was to lose all of his. The assessment report says the plan "identified six individuals who would lose access to the land and thereby to their source of income", one fewer than the plan counts. During implementation, seven project-affected persons were compensated: US$13,005 in all, made up of US$4,806 for the direct loss of harvest, US$1,772 for income support and US$6,427 for restoration of income. The assessment report says no issues were reported on the resettlement safeguard and that the status reports rated resettlement performance satisfactory throughout. The completion report, three years earlier, says only that compensation payments due for involuntary resettlement were completed in a timely manner and that all compensation due was calculated and paid to the affected people; it gives no numbers.
sao-gabriel-cable-station-urban-farmers.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 40 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. No document records anyone relocated. The counts are of people who lost access to land they farmed: seven in the resettlement plan, seven compensated.
sao-gabriel-cable-station-urban-farmers.outcome: The project closed on 31 December 2014. The assessment report of 4 June 2018 records the compensation as paid and no outstanding resettlement issues.

sao-gabriel-cable-station-urban-farmers.confidence_note: The figures come from the lender's own field-based assessment report, which is the only document that counts the people affected; the completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of it carry no numbers. No independent account was found. The assessment report says the resettlement plan identified six individuals who would lose access to the land; the plan itself says seven and prints seven data sheets, so the six is the assessment report's error about the document it cites. The seven is the plan's own census of the farmers who would lose land, which the assessment report then records as compensated. kumasi-lands-office-farmers-displaced.title: Six farmers lose the land they worked to the Kumasi lands office site
kumasi-lands-office-farmers-displaced.point: Kumasi, from Nominatim. The completion report names Kumasi as the site of the regional head office but does not give the plot.

lenders.name: World Bank (International Development Association)
lenders.role: Project P120636, Second Land Administration Project. IDA Credit 48700, US$50 million, of which US$46,795,104 was disbursed; Trust Fund TF-14256, US$2,879,706, of which US$2,500,919 was disbursed; and IDA 63450, US$35 million, of which nothing was disbursed. Approved 31 March 2011, effective 8 August 2011, mid-term review 2 June 2014, original closing 31 March 2016, actual closing 20 January 2020 (completion report ICR00005225, 18 June 2020, which revises an earlier completion report of 19 October 2018). The US$5 million of government counterpart funding was not provided in full: less than US$1 million was disbursed. Environmental category B, partial assessment. Two safeguard policies were triggered: Environmental Assessment (OP 4.01) and Involuntary Resettlement (OP 4.12). The revised completion report rates the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, where the earlier completion report of 19 October 2018 rated it Moderately Satisfactory; it gives the reason as the failure of the project and the Lands Commission to address the bottlenecks in deeds and title registration and to meet the outcome indicators, which leaves efficacy Modest. The Evaluation Group reviewed both reports: its review of 22 March 2019 and its review dated 31 December 2020 in the Bank's archive record each rate the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory.

companies.name: Lands Commission, Ghana
companies.role: The state body that manages public land and keeps the land register, under the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources. The regional head office built at Kumasi under the project was its office.

companies.name: Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, Ghana
companies.role: The ministry that held the project coordination unit and, with the Lands Commission, implemented the project.

kumasi-lands-office-farmers-displaced.community: The project built a regional head office for the land sector agencies at Kumasi, on undeveloped government land. The revised completion report says the environmental and social assessment prepared for that land covered a site "which caused economic displacement of six (6) farmers", and that although the project did not physically displace anyone it economically displaced six farmers, so an Abbreviated Resettlement Action Plan was prepared. The six is the resettlement plan's own count. The abbreviated plan surveyed the Kumasi site on 11 and 12 October 2010 and found six farmers there, one woman and five men aged between 28 and 65, two of them keeping pigs and the rest growing cassava, plantain and maize, earning between GH¢10 and GH¢400 a month; it records that they knew they would have to move their activities before the civil works began and that they wanted cash compensation for the loss of their farms. The appraisal document of March 2011 carried the same figure, and noted that people occupying the land earmarked for the office could lose their livelihood. The revised completion report of 2020 is the document that attaches a completed harm to the figure, saying the site "caused economic displacement of six (6) farmers" and that the project "involved economic displacement of six farmers". The report says the resettlement activities on economic displacement and livelihood restoration were carried out with proper disclosure of information and the involvement of stakeholders and that no issues arose, and that based on reports and evidence from the field the resettlement was in compliance with the lender's policies. The plan put the whole resettlement budget at GH¢9,432.70. No outcome document says what the six farmers were paid. The first completion report, of 19 October 2018, does not mention the six farmers at all: it says only that the two safeguard policies were triggered and that no issues arose during implementation. The construction at Kumasi was delayed, and the completion report names those delays, with the land information system contract, as the clear exceptions to otherwise adequate project management.
kumasi-lands-office-farmers-displaced.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 36 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The completion report says there was no physical displacement; the six is a count of farmers economically displaced.
kumasi-lands-office-farmers-displaced.outcome: The project closed on 20 January 2020. The completion report records the resettlement as complete and the safeguards rating as Satisfactory at the time the project's main activities finished in January 2019.

kumasi-lands-office-farmers-displaced.confidence_note: The six is the October 2010 resettlement plan's own count of the farmers on the site, repeated in the appraisal document; the only outcome document that records the displacement as having happened is the lender's revised completion report of 2020, followed by the Evaluation Group's review of it. senegal-river-perimeter-crops-destroyed.title: Crops destroyed with no compensation paid in a Mauritanian irrigation perimeter, and two seasons of crops lost in Mali
senegal-river-perimeter-crops-destroyed.place: An unnamed irrigation perimeter in the Senegal River valley, Mauritania
senegal-river-perimeter-crops-destroyed.point: Kaédi, Gorgol, from Nominatim. The appraisal document places the project's Mauritanian works in the Gorgol and Trarza wilayas and lists an intake rehabilitation and a weir at Kaédi. The completion report does not name the perimeter where the crops were destroyed.

lenders.name: World Bank (International Development Association)
lenders.role: Project P093826, Senegal River Basin Multi-purpose Water Resources Development Project, first phase of an adaptable programme. IDA Credit 41820 to Mali, SDR 21.0 million (about US$30.08 million equivalent); IDA Credit 41830 to Mauritania, SDR 22.2 million (about US$31.78 million); IDA Credit 41840 to Senegal, SDR 21.0 million (about US$30.08 million); IDA Grant H2310 to Guinea, SDR 12.60 million (about US$18.04 million); and Dutch Trust Fund grant TF-94727, SDR 8.5 million (about US$12.12 million). Original commitment SDR 76.80 million, of which SDR 68.01 million was disbursed. Approved 8 June 2006, effective 14 March 2007, restructured 17 June 2011, closing date extended from 8 September 2011 to 31 March 2013 (completion report ICR2653, 25 September 2013). Environmental category A. The completion report lists ten safeguard policies as triggered: Environmental Assessment (OP/BP/GP 4.01), Natural Habitats (OP/BP 4.04), Pest Management (OP 4.09), Cultural Property (OP 4.11), Involuntary Resettlement (OP/BP 4.12), Indigenous Peoples (OP 4.10), Forests (OP/BP 4.36), Safety of Dams (OP/BP 4.37), Projects in Disputed Areas (OP/BP/GP 7.60) and Projects on International Waterways (OP/BP/GP 7.50). The appraisal document's own table of policies triggered marks two of those ten in the No column, Indigenous Peoples (then OD 4.20, being revised as OP 4.10) and Projects in Disputed Areas (OP/BP/GP 7.60); no document reconciles that with the completion report's list of ten. The report rates the outcome Satisfactory, risk to development outcome Moderate, and Bank and borrower performance Satisfactory. The Evaluation Group's review of 30 June 2015 rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Unsatisfactory, borrower performance Moderately Satisfactory, and the quality of the completion report Unsatisfactory.

companies.name: Organisation pour la Mise en Valeur du fleuve Sénégal (OMVS)
companies.role: The river basin organisation of Guinea, Mali, Mauritania and Senegal, and the project's implementing agency. Its project unit held the safeguards specialist and supervised the national executing agencies. Its own completion assessors recorded the destroyed crops in Mauritania.

companies.name: Société Nationale pour le Développement Rural (SONADER), Mauritania
companies.role: The national rural development company, the executing agency for the hydro-agricultural works in Mauritania. The completion report records procurement delays at SONADER for want of a procurement specialist.

senegal-river-perimeter-crops-destroyed.community: The credits paid for water intakes, pumping stations, canals and the rehabilitation of irrigated land in the Senegal River basin: more than 4,400 hectares rehabilitated or newly developed, 88 kilometres of canals and 47 pumping stations. The completion report says safeguards work in the field often went to environmental questions at the expense of social ones, and that some issues were not tracked effectively: "For example in one perimeter in Mauritania the OMVS completion assessors noted that crops had been destroyed by the implementation of the project and no compensation had been paid." The same paragraph says contractors needed regular follow-up to keep up basic measures such as sanitation for labourers, that executing agencies met their responsibilities in most cases, and that local people spoke well of some mitigation measures, including walkways that cut the time and cost of reaching markets. In Mali, delays in rehabilitating agricultural land cost farmers their crops over two seasons, and the national executing agency distributed food directly to them. The basin organisation's own report, printed as an annex to the completion report under the activities the credits financed, repeats both findings, writing that it was the winter crops that were destroyed, and adds that there were no land disputes after the irrigation areas were rehabilitated. The report does not say how many people lost crops in either country.
senegal-river-perimeter-crops-destroyed.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 36 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. No document counts anyone relocated, and no document counts the people whose crops were destroyed.
senegal-river-perimeter-crops-destroyed.outcome: The project closed on 31 March 2013. The completion report records the destroyed crops as uncompensated and does not say whether anything was paid afterwards. The Evaluation Group's review does not mention the destroyed crops, and says that despite the project being category A the completion report gives no clear statement of safeguard compliance.

senegal-river-perimeter-crops-destroyed.confidence_note: The finding is the lender's own, in the completion report and repeated in the basin organisation's annex to it. No independent account was found. The report names neither the perimeter nor the number of people whose crops were destroyed, and the sentence sits in a paragraph that otherwise reports compliance as satisfactory. The Evaluation Group's review of the same project says "The PAD identified the project as a Category 'A' project, and the OP/BP 4.01 was triggered" and names no other policy, where the completion report lists ten and the appraisal document's own table marks eight of the ten in the Yes column. The review also paraphrases the sentence immediately before the destroyed-crops finding, that safeguards work in the field went to physical issues at the expense of social ones, and stops short of the example that follows it.

bijilo-cable-route-compensation-unpaid.title: Compensation paid to six of the fifteen on the Bijilo cable route in The Gambia
bijilo-cable-route-compensation-unpaid.place: Cable route from Bijilo Beach to the Sukuta institutional area along the Kombo Beach Highway, Bijilo, West Coast Region, The Gambia
bijilo-cable-route-compensation-unpaid.point: Bijilo, from Nominatim. The resettlement plan says all the affected activities are in Bijilo, along the cable route from Bijilo Beach to the Sukuta institutional area.

lenders.name: World Bank (International Development Association)
lenders.role: Project P122402, West Africa Regional Communications Infrastructure Project, second project under the first phase (WARCIP APL 1B). IDA Grant H7130 to The Gambia, US$35 million, of which US$32,563,720 was disbursed; IDA Grant H7120 to Burkina Faso, US$23 million, of which US$19,948,274 was disbursed; IDA Grant H7140 to Guinea, US$34 million, of which US$31,755,664 was disbursed; and IDA Credit 62220 to Burkina Faso, US$20 million, of which US$16,651,819 was disbursed. Approved 21 June 2011, effective 31 October 2011, mid-term review 2 June 2014, original closing 31 December 2016, actual closing 30 July 2021 (completion report ICR00005569, 25 February 2022). Environmental category B. Four safeguard policies were triggered, which the completion report names as Environmental Assessment (OP/BP 4.01), Natural Habitats (OP/BP 4.36), Physical Cultural Resources (OP/BP 4.11) and Involuntary Resettlement (OP/BP 4.12). The completion report rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, and the Evaluation Group's review, dated 23 August 2022 in the Bank's archive record, agrees.

companies.name: Ministry of Information and Communication Infrastructure (MOICI), The Gambia
companies.role: The ministry made responsible by the resettlement plan for carrying it out, through the state telecommunications company. The completion report names the dispute between the two over who should release the funds as the main cause of the delay.

companies.name: Gambia Telecommunications Company Limited (GAMTEL)
companies.role: The state telecommunications company through which the ministry was to implement the resettlement plan.

companies.name: SAL Consult Limited
companies.role: The Accra consultancy that wrote The Gambia resettlement plan of May 2011, which counted the people the cable route would affect.

bijilo-cable-route-compensation-unpaid.community: The cable route in The Gambia runs from Bijilo Beach to the Sukuta institutional area along the Kombo Beach Highway, past houses, shops, workshops, petrol stations, empty plots and a hotel. The resettlement plan of May 2011 listed 27 structures or plots and said 27 people would be affected, with no permanent or temporary structure lost and no land acquisition needed; it described the effects as temporary inconvenience. The completion report says that in June 2013, two years after the plan was written, implementation had not started, and that the number of people affected was then listed as 15, entitled to about US$1,500 in all. That 15 is also the plan's figure, and in the plan it is not a count of people: the plan says it "covered 15 shops and 4 residential houses which will be impacted by the project", and its Annex 1 lists 15 entitlement entries by initials or trading name — among them a petrol station, an inn, a lumber shop, a charcoal and firewood seller and two concrete-products sites — with a disturbance allowance and assistance for each and a total of 37,923.49 dalasi. The completion report gives the same 15 as a count of people affected. A year later the payments were still not finished. Radio announcements in local languages and repeated visits followed, and "Compensation was provided to the six people who were located." A footnote cites a monitoring report of 7 October 2014 from the ministry and a supervision mission report of January 2015 acknowledging payment to just six of the 15. The report says many of the others had moved away and that different businesses were on the sites. The report also finds no documentation that the contractor applied the environmental management plan, and none that the environmental and social measures for the operating phase were adopted. In Burkina Faso, the works from Ouagadougou to Paga partly affected structures and caused temporary loss of revenue: 277 households were identified as affected and 274 received money, FCFA 23 million or about US$40,000, and the report adds that the resettlement completion report said all compensation measures had been carried out. On the Dindéogo to Zabré extension, 198 households were affected and all 198 were paid, FCFA 19 million or about US$33,000. The works between Fada and Pama were not built, for security reasons.
bijilo-cable-route-compensation-unpaid.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 27 for this project, which is not a count of people moved. The May 2011 resettlement plan also gives 27, and gives it twice over: a census that "confirmed that no more than 27 persons may be affected", and a table of "27 structures/ plots of land" along the route that includes two empty plots, three uncompleted structures, an uninhabited structure and a security zone. No document records anyone relocated. The Gambia figure changed during implementation from 27 to 15, and compensation reached six.
bijilo-cable-route-compensation-unpaid.outcome: The project closed on 30 July 2021 with compensation paid to six of the 15 entries on The Gambia plan's compensation annex and not to the rest. The Evaluation Group's review repeats the six of 15 and adds that, according to the project team, only six could be identified after an extensive campaign and that the actions taken were appropriate and sufficient; that is a statement by staff and not a document.

bijilo-cable-route-compensation-unpaid.confidence_note: The unpaid compensation is recorded in the lender's own completion report, which cites a government monitoring report and two mission reports by date for the payment to six of 15 people. Those underlying reports are not public. No independent account was found. The 15 is the plan's own figure, which the plan attaches to shops and houses and to the 15 rows of its compensation annex, and which the completion report and the review both carry as a count of people; the unit shifts between the documents and neither explains it. The people are identified in the plan's annex by initials or trading name but are not named in any outcome document, and the report's stated reason for the failure to pay is that the others could not be found. The three households of 277 in Burkina Faso that are not recorded as paid sit one sentence from the statement that all compensation measures were carried out, and no document reconciles the two.

lalara-fibre-assets-destroyed.title: Assets destroyed and left uncompensated on the Gabon fibre route at Lalara
lalara-fibre-assets-destroyed.place: Lalara, on the fibre optic route from Booué to Oyem, Gabon
lalara-fibre-assets-destroyed.point: Lalara village, from Nominatim, which places it in Woleu-Ntem. The completion report and the Evaluation Group's review both place Lalara in Ogooué-Ivindo Province. The loan agreement lists Lalara on the fibre link the loan financed.

lenders.name: World Bank (International Bank for Reconstruction and Development)
lenders.role: Project P122776, fourth phase of the Central African Backbone Program, Gabon (CAB4). IBRD Loan 81500, US$58 million, of which US$55,739,093 was disbursed, and IBRD Loan 86290, EUR 20.2 million or about US$23 million equivalent, of which US$23,195,506 was disbursed. Approved 28 March 2012, effective 6 March 2013, mid-term review 30 January 2015, original closing 31 December 2016, actual closing 31 October 2020 (completion report ICR00005105, 9 April 2021). The completion report's financing table shows the US$51 million of government counterpart financing recorded at appraisal revised to nil, with nothing disbursed; the Evaluation Group's review says that, on information the project team gave it, the government's actual contribution was US$53.1 million, of which US$51 million on the original project. Neither document reconciles the two. Five safeguard policies were triggered: Environmental Assessment (OP 4.01), Natural Habitats (OP 4.04), Indigenous Peoples (OP 4.10), Physical Cultural Resources (OP 4.11) and Involuntary Resettlement (OP 4.12). The completion report rates the overall outcome Satisfactory, and says the safeguards rating was lowered to Moderately Satisfactory in the final status report. The Evaluation Group's review, dated 21 June 2021 in the Bank's archive record, records the same safeguards finding.

companies.name: Commission Nationale des Travaux d'Intérêt Public pour la Promotion de l'Entrepreneuriat et de l'Emploi (CN-TIPPEE)
companies.role: The public works commission that was the project's implementing unit, responsible for the works, the grievance mechanism and the resettlement and indigenous peoples plans.

lalara-fibre-assets-destroyed.community: The loans paid for fibre optic links including Booué to Koumameyong, Lalara, Mitzic, Oyem, Bitam and the Cameroon border. The completion report says the project's overall safeguards rating was lowered to Moderately Satisfactory in the final status report for three reasons: delays in the safeguards audit; "social risks associated with non-compensation for the accidental destruction of assets during fieldwork in Lalara"; and incomplete implementation of the Indigenous Peoples Plan in the field. A footnote adds that the construction operators were asked to compensate those destructions but had not done so by the closing date, "raising the prospects of complaints from people whose assets were destroyed". A second footnote says some indigenous peoples activities were still not carried out. The grievance mechanism was working at the closing date and followed the two environmental and social management plans, but its last revision did not cover gender-based violence. 168 complaints were received, 41 per cent of them about loss of revenue and stalls, and 129 had been resolved by the date of a unit report of 11 March 2021. The government's own account, printed in the completion report, says counterpart funds of around FCFA 3 billion made it possible to compensate project-affected persons, repair non-conformities and finish the works, and that local communities helped resolve complaints during resettlement operations and provided land for the technical centres. No document counts the people whose assets were destroyed at Lalara.
lalara-fibre-assets-destroyed.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 13 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. No document counts anyone relocated.
lalara-fibre-assets-destroyed.outcome: The project closed on 31 October 2020 with the Lalara destructions uncompensated and the Indigenous Peoples Plan unfinished, and with 129 of the 168 complaints recorded as resolved in a project unit report of 11 March 2021 and the rest still being processed. The Evaluation Group's review says both the Lalara compensation and the indigenous peoples issue were still unresolved when it was written, attributing that to the project team rather than to a document.

lalara-fibre-assets-destroyed.confidence_note: The destruction of assets and the failure to pay for it are recorded only in the lender's own completion report, in its main text and a footnote, and repeated in the Evaluation Group's review of it. No independent account was found. No document counts the people affected or says what was destroyed. The two documents disagree on the complaints: the completion report says 168 complaints were received, 41 per cent of them about loss of revenue and stalls, while the review says all 168 related to loss of revenue. Lalara is placed in Ogooué-Ivindo Province by both documents and in Woleu-Ntem by Nominatim.

tema-ouagadougou-bamako-corridor-compens.title: Road corridor works begun before compensation was finished in Burkina Faso, with seven households resettled in Mali
tema-ouagadougou-bamako-corridor-compens.place: Ouagadougou to Sakoinsé section of National Road 1, Burkina Faso, on the Tema to Ouagadougou to Bamako corridor
tema-ouagadougou-bamako-corridor-compens.point: Sakoinsé village, Kokologo, Boulkiemdé, from Nominatim. It is the end of the Ouagadougou to Sakoinsé road section the credit rehabilitated and the section the abbreviated compensation plan covers.

lenders.name: World Bank (International Development Association)
lenders.role: Project P079749, West Africa Regional Transport and Transit Facilitation Project. IDA Credits 44350 (Mali), 44380 (Burkina Faso) and 44390 (Ghana), original commitment SDR 116.70 million, revised SDR 116.00 million, of which SDR 115.43 million was disbursed. Approved 19 June 2008, closing date 30 June 2015 (completion report ICR00003592, 31 December 2015; Financing Agreements for Credit 4438-BF conformed 8 July 2008, Credit 4439-GH conformed 11 July 2008 and Credit 4435-ML conformed 17 July 2008). Environmental category B. Two safeguard policies were triggered: Environmental Assessment (OP/BP/GP 4.01) and Involuntary Resettlement (OP/BP 4.12); the Evaluation Group's assessment report says the second was triggered only for minor land acquisition or loss of income from the road rehabilitation or the construction of the rest stops. The completion report rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, risk to development outcome Moderate, Bank performance Satisfactory and borrower performance Moderately Satisfactory. The Evaluation Group's field-based assessment report of 19 April 2018 rates borrower performance moderately satisfactory and says the supervision of safeguards was satisfactory. Parallel financing came from the African Development Bank, the European Union and the West African Development Bank.

companies.name: Ministère des Infrastructures, des Transports et de l'Habitat, Burkina Faso
companies.role: The ministry whose directorate general of roads held the Burkina Faso works, applied the delay penalty clause to the Ouagadougou to Sakoinsé contractor and was responsible for the compensation plan for that section.

companies.name: Ministère de l'Équipement et des Transports, Mali
companies.role: The ministry that published the compensation and resettlement framework for the Malian sections of the corridor and held the Bamako to Bougouni and Sikasso to Hérémakono works.

companies.name: Ghana Highway Authority
companies.role: The roads agency, under Ghana's transport ministry, responsible for the Ghanaian corridor works and the land acquisition for the rest stops.

tema-ouagadougou-bamako-corridor-compens.community: The credits rehabilitated road sections on the corridor from the port of Tema in Ghana through Ouagadougou to Bamako, and were to build rest stops. The completion report says that "the compensations were fully carried out, albeit with delays. Particularly in Burkina Faso, the works contract was signed while the compensations were still ongoing." In Ghana an increase in the financing let the resettlement and compensation, first budgeted from government funds, be paid faster. "In the case of Mali, involuntary resettlements were made for seven households. The compensations were fully financed from the counterpart funding resources." The Evaluation Group's field-based assessment report says all compensation payments were made, with delays in Burkina Faso and Ghana caused by government budget limits, that in Mali seven households were resettled and compensation was timely, and that "no information was obtained on how many people were compensated in Burkina Faso and Ghana". It names slow land acquisition in Ghana for the rest stops as the only shortcoming of the safeguards work. The abbreviated compensation plan for the Ouagadougou to Sakoinsé section, written in October 2007, names four people losing a hectare of land each and 800 kilogrammes of harvest a year at borrow pit 4 and at Douré and Sakoinsé, and lists trees lost at two other borrow pits. The borrower's own report, printed as an annex to the completion report, lists delays in payment of compensation and counterpart funds, and land acquisition, among the project's challenges.
tema-ouagadougou-bamako-corridor-compens.killed_note: The completion report says the road safety measures considerably reduced the number of accidents along the corridor without reaching the targets, and the borrower's annex says the speed humps built on the Ouagadougou to Sakoinsé section reduced deaths on that stretch. Neither document records a death caused by the works.
tema-ouagadougou-bamako-corridor-compens.displaced_label: 7 households resettled in Mali, from the completion report (paragraph 67, 31 December 2015) and the Evaluation Group's assessment report (paragraph 4.6, 19 April 2018)
tema-ouagadougou-bamako-corridor-compens.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 9 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The seven households are the only count of people resettled in any document; the assessment report says no information was obtained on how many people were compensated in Burkina Faso or Ghana.
tema-ouagadougou-bamako-corridor-compens.outcome: The project closed on 30 June 2015. Both the completion report and the assessment report record all the compensation as eventually paid. The transit facilitation part of the project failed: the three countries never agreed on the customs arrangements.

tema-ouagadougou-bamako-corridor-compens.confidence_note: All of it comes from the lender's own documents: the completion report, the Evaluation Group's field-based assessment report and its review of the completion report. No independent account was found. The seven households in Mali are counted but not placed: no document says which road section they lived on. The finding that works began in Burkina Faso while compensation was still being paid carries no count of the people affected, and both documents say the compensation was finished in the end.

drc-rn5-rn6-rn2-compensation-arrears.title: Resettled people inadequately compensated on the Congo road works, with 61 per cent of the National Road 2 payments made at closing
drc-rn5-rn6-rn2-compensation-arrears.place: National Road 6 from Akula to Gemena, Mbari, Libenge and Zongo, Équateur, and National Road 5 from Lubumbashi to Kasomeno and Kasenga, Katanga, Democratic Republic of the Congo
drc-rn5-rn6-rn2-compensation-arrears.point: Gemena, from Nominatim. It is on the National Road 6 stretch the grant rehabilitated. The completion report does not say which road segments the compensation findings cover.

lenders.name: World Bank (International Development Association)
lenders.role: Project P088619, Emergency Living Conditions Improvement Support Project (ELCISP). IDA Grant H1640, SDR 53.90 million, of which SDR 53.87 million was disbursed. Approved 26 May 2005, original closing 30 September 2010, actual closing 30 June 2012 after three restructurings, the last on 22 February 2012 (completion report ICR2521, 21 December 2012). Environmental category B. Five safeguard policies were triggered: Environmental Assessment (OP 4.01), Natural Habitats (OP 4.04), Physical Cultural Resources (OP 4.11), Indigenous Peoples (OP 4.10) and Involuntary Resettlement (OP 4.12). The completion report rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, risk to development outcome High, and Bank and borrower performance Moderately Satisfactory. The Evaluation Group's review of 23 September 2013 rates implementing agency performance Moderately Unsatisfactory and overall borrower performance Moderately Unsatisfactory, and says that on the information given it cannot be concluded that there was compliance with the environmental safeguard policies.

companies.name: Unité de Coordination de Projets (UCoP), Democratic Republic of the Congo
companies.role: The government project coordination unit that implemented the project. The completion report says a lack of oversight by it led to the corruption case the Bank's integrity unit investigated, and the borrower's own report names inadequate monitoring of environmental and social aspects during construction among the weaknesses a technical audit found.

companies.name: Bureau Central de Coordination (BCECO), Democratic Republic of the Congo
companies.role: One of the delegated contract managers for the works; it was trained by an international environmental and social consulting firm hired after the mid-term review.

drc-rn5-rn6-rn2-compensation-arrears.community: The grant rehabilitated National Road 6 from Akula through Gemena and Mbari to Libenge and Zongo in Équateur and National Road 5 from Lubumbashi through Kasomeno to Kasenga in Katanga, and funded urban works in several towns. The completion report says the mid-term review "revealed that project affected persons resettled due to the road construction were not adequately compensated, that the works contracts did not, as foreseen, include funding to mitigate environmental aspects, and that the problem of medical wastes from health facilities funded by the project was not fully taken into account". An international environmental and social consulting firm was then hired to train the project unit, the contractors and the delegated contract manager, and management plans were drawn up for each 30-kilometre road segment. A total of 627 project-affected persons were compensated. At project closing the beneficiary satisfaction survey found no adequate solution to the medical waste. The report also covers National Road 2, rehabilitated under an earlier Bank-financed project: no displacement or asset losses occurred there, but the road shoulders were cut back, leaving almost no space between the road and neighbouring buildings and raising the risk of traffic accidents. An after-the-fact resettlement plan was prepared for that road and was to be paid for by this project, but a change in the lender's rules stopped cash compensation being paid from its funds. The government has implemented the plan as money became available and had paid 61 per cent of the amount due to 35 project-affected persons. The amount is given as US$262,090 in the completion report and as US$202,090 in the Evaluation Group's review. The Group's review adds that an indigenous peoples plan was prepared and circulated to non-governmental organisations, academics, Pygmy associations and news agencies, and that no information is given on whether it was carried out.
drc-rn5-rn6-rn2-compensation-arrears.killed_note: No document records a death caused by the works. The completion report says the reduced shoulders on National Road 2 increase the risk of traffic accidents.
drc-rn5-rn6-rn2-compensation-arrears.displaced_note: ICIJ gives no displacement estimate for this project. No document counts people relocated. The 627 is a count of project-affected persons compensated, and the 35 a count of people owed money for the earlier National Road 2 works.
drc-rn5-rn6-rn2-compensation-arrears.outcome: The project closed on 30 June 2012. At that point 61 per cent of the National Road 2 compensation had been paid to 35 people and the rest was being paid by the government as funds allowed; the medical waste problem was unsolved. The completion report also records a corruption case investigated by the lender's integrity unit, and an advance of US$1.4 million on a road contract cancelled in 2010 for non-performance that had still not been repaid when the report was written.

drc-rn5-rn6-rn2-compensation-arrears.confidence_note: The findings are the lender's own, in the completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of it, with the borrower's annex agreeing that monitoring of environmental and social aspects during construction was inadequate. No independent account was found. The people resettled and inadequately compensated are not counted: the 627 is a count of people compensated, not of people underpaid. The two documents give different totals for the National Road 2 plan, US$262,090 and US$202,090, and neither reconciles them. The reduced road shoulders on National Road 2 were the work of the earlier project, not this one; what belongs to this project is the unpaid balance of the plan it was restructured to finance.

p103189-africa-stockpiles-mali.drop_reason: Africa Stockpiles Programme Project 1, Mali. The resettlement plan of November 2010 for the Nanguila pesticide store says the opposite of a displacement: "vu qu'aucune activite a caractere economique et social n'est situee dans ce rayon, il n'y aura pas de deplacement physique (ni de personne ni de bien) sur le site". Its 170 is a plan estimate: "Il a ete identifie au moins huit familles totalisant environ 170 personnes, qui seront directement affectees par le projet", eight families around the store at Nanguila, which is also where ICIJ's 170 comes from. Checked in the outcome documents: the completion report of 28 June 2013 says at paragraph 27 that a resettlement action plan was prepared for safeguarding and soil remediation works at Nanguila "which involved the temporary relocation of inhabitants during the cleanup operation", that it was approved, disclosed in November 2010 and "subsequently implemented in full compliance with safeguard requirements". No count of people moved, no payment shortfall, no loss. Its safeguards count sentence at paragraph 24 says the project triggered two policies, Environmental Assessment and Pest Management, while paragraph 27 reports compliance with Involuntary Resettlement. The Evaluation Group's review of 27 March 2015 and the Group's assessment report of 29 September 2016 do not mention Nanguila. The borrower section of the completion report for Mali carries no separate account of the resettlement.

p104716-liberia-agriculture-infrastructu.drop_reason: Liberia Agriculture and Infrastructure Development Project. Checked in the outcome documents: the completion report of 26 January 2016 says at page 25 that "in the case of the squatters to be resettled from Vai Town bridge construction, the government expeditiously implemented the safeguards policy and funds for compensation were released in a timely manner", and at page 14 that the project complied with the requirements of all safeguards policies. The Evaluation Group's review of 8 July 2016 repeats both. Neither document counts anyone moved, and neither records a payment shortfall or any other loss. The counts are in the plan only: the Environmental Management and Resettlement Management Plan of 4 August 2008 for the Vai Town bridge lists three affected houses, shops, 26 squatter households comprising 128 persons renting rooms in three squatter houses, four households in makeshift structures of their own and eleven petty traders who are not residents. ICIJ's 147 comes from that plan.

p115664-emergency-monrovia-urban-sanitat.drop_reason: Emergency Monrovia Urban Sanitation Project, Liberia. Checked in the outcome documents: the completion report of 20 June 2017 says at paragraph 40 that two abbreviated resettlement action plans were prepared, one for the Fiamah and Stockton Creek waste transfer stations and one for the Whein Town landfill buffer zone, and that "Compensation was paid with no outstanding issues". No count of people moved and no payment shortfall anywhere in the report. What the report does record is environmental and engagement failure: no dedicated staff at the project unit or the contractors to oversee the environmental plans, water and leachate sampling stopped in 2014 during the Ebola crisis and resumed only at the Bank's request in December 2016, engagement with the Whein Town community weak and the grievance mechanism non-existent, two instances of vandalism at the landfill, and complaints from people living around the landfill and transfer stations about odour, litter and mosquitoes that were not followed up. The December 2016 water analysis "showed no major deterioration in water quality in comparison to results recorded in the baseline study". The Evaluation Group's review of 29 September 2017 repeats all of this. Odour, litter and mosquitoes with no count of people and no loss of land, livelihood or service is not a documented harm to identifiable people under the forward rule. ICIJ gives 143.

p122065-waapp-1c-togo.drop_reason: West Africa Agricultural Productivity Program APL 1C, Togo. Checked in the outcome document: the completion report of 19 June 2020 says at paragraph 88 that "The World Bank's involuntary resettlement policy was triggered, but no negative social impacts occurred." Paragraph 87 records the one adverse finding: "In some countries, the implementation of subproject ESMPs underscored difficulties in maintaining hygiene, health, and safety standards, including the low use of personal protective equipment, absence of fire extinguishers, failure to register employees with the National Social Security Fund, absence of medical first aid, and absence of sanitary facilities for employees." It names no country, no subproject and no number of workers, so there are no identifiable people. The Evaluation Group's review of 14 September 2020 adds nothing on either point. ICIJ gives 136.

p108941-west-africa-regional-fisheries.drop_reason: West Africa Regional Fisheries Program, first phase. Checked in the outcome document: the completion report of 12 May 2017 says at paragraph 45 that the infrastructure works in Cabo Verde, Senegal and Sierra Leone "were scaled down, dropped or did not move forward", and that the only safeguards omissions were on minor works: "in Senegal, alternative livelihoods and the construction of fishers' houses were carried out without screening for impacts and subsequent safeguards instruments but since the works were very small, there were no complaints or consequences". The Sierra Leone landing site at Kissy Dockyard, where the Bank had reported significant squatter settlements and a resettlement action plan was launched, was abandoned in February 2012 when the government moved the site to Murray Town, which then turned out to be a Ramsar wetland; the project closed before those works began. No count of people moved, no payment shortfall, no land taken. The project's enforcement component records arrests: offence notification or arrest of 449 vessels out of 287 industrial and 7,395 small-scale vessels inspected, and 16 arrests recorded by the joint maritime committee. Those are arrests of vessels for illegal fishing, the project's own intended output, and no document records anyone detained by the project or harmed by its enforcement. ICIJ gives 118.

p104456-cameroon-energy-sector-developme.drop_reason: Cameroon Energy Sector Development Project. Checked in the outcome documents. The completion report of 27 December 2017 says at paragraph 64 that "The compensation decrees were signed in 2015 with a delay of more than two years due to the complex and lengthy compensation process in Cameroon. The compensation campaigns for the 20 departments were completed between April and December 2015. The compensation campaigns were well managed and allowed the payment of compensation of between 92 and 100 percent of the PAPs depending on the department or region (a small percentage of PAPs could not be compensated because they could not be found)." That is a recorded shortfall, but it carries no count of people, no site, no identified case, and the stated reason is that the people could not be located; the same paragraph says the impact assessments and resettlement plans were prepared for all three regions and that the project complied with all the measures the environmental and resettlement plans required. The works started in November 2015, after compensation was concluded, in both regions where the grid extension was built. No other document adds a figure: the Evaluation Group's review of 10 May 2018 records only that publication of the compensation decrees caused extensive delays to the rural electrification works. That is thinner than the standing limb (b) edge, which requires identified cases at a named site. Also checked: the project financed only preparatory activities for the Lom Pangar Hydropower Project, which the completion report says triggered no safeguard policies, so nothing at Lom Pangar belongs to this credit. ICIJ gives 52.

p071391-nigeria-second-urban-water.drop_reason: Nigeria Second National Urban Water Sector Reform Project. Checked in the outcome documents: the completion report of 21 May 2018 says at paragraph 52, in full, "A Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF) was prepared in and disclosed in 2005, followed by site specific Resettlement Action plans (for the additional sites after restructuring in March 2012). Delays in payments to Project Affected People in Lagos led to a brief suspension of works in February 2017, but this was quickly resolved by April 2017." Paragraph 50 says the major safeguard documents were compiled, approved and disclosed in time and that "no major violations are on record". The Evaluation Group's review of 17 July 2018 repeats the two-month suspension and its resolution. There is no count of people, no site beyond the city, and the only recorded consequence of the delay is the suspension of the civil works, which is the pattern that decided a drop in round 19. The borrower's completion report, cited in the completion report, finds that the safeguards function's impact "has not been significantly felt" and that "documentation of safeguards implementation activities was weak"; both are process findings with no person attached. ICIJ gives 16.

p083751-west-central-africa-air-transpor.drop_reason: West and Central Africa Air Transport Safety and Security Project. Checked in the outcome document: the completion report of 12 December 2014 says at paragraph 63 that Involuntary Resettlement was triggered by the fencing of airport security perimeters, the removal of vegetable gardens inside those perimeters and the removal of a few structures built inside them, at Conakry, Douala and Yaoundé. Paragraph 64 says "all three RAPs and other environmental mitigation measures were fully and successfully implemented". Paragraph 65 gives the outcome country by country: in Burkina Faso "Plant sellers along 'Patte d'Oie' roundabout in the airport security perimeter were satisfactorily relocated, and supported by a compensation process executed in compliance with The World Bank safeguards"; in Guinea "All farming activities have been satisfactorily relocated", with a compensation process the report calls transparent; in Cameroon the relocation of a religious shrine one kilometre from the Yaoundé airport fence, flagged in the resettlement plan, did not happen because the government built a new access road around it; in Mali there were no environmental or social issues. No outcome document counts a single person or household moved, and none records a payment shortfall or a loss. The Evaluation Group's review of 1 June 2015 adds nothing. ICIJ gives 7.

p087004-cape-verde-road-sector-support.drop_reason: Cape Verde Road Sector Support Project. Checked in the outcome documents: the completion report of 28 May 2014 says at paragraph 38 that the original project required no land acquisition, that during implementation the alignment of the Alcatraz to Figueira road on Maio island was slightly modified and "required minor land acquisition of uncultivated agricultural land", that works on the Ponta de Talho to Igreja road under the second additional financing "required partial acquisition of agricultural plots", and that an abbreviated resettlement plan "was prepared, disclosed and satisfactorily implemented". No count of people in any outcome document, and no payment shortfall. The named people are in the plan only: the abbreviated plan of 1 June 2012 lists individual landowners with the area each lost, in square metres, and the value calculated for each. The Evaluation Group's review of 27 October 2014 adds that the Vila das Pombas road and bridge works, where the appraisal expected minor land taking of stonewalls, were to be paid for from the borrower's own funds and that the completion report does not report compliance in those areas. ICIJ gives 7.

p130184-warcip-benin.drop_reason: WARCIP APL 1C, Benin. Checked in the outcome documents: the completion report of 12 January 2018 says at paragraph 106 that by 2 April 2015, when the ACE cable landed on the Benin coast, the government "had executed all social and environmental plans satisfactorily, including adequate information sharing and compensation of all individuals and businesses along the cable route". The Evaluation Group's review of 27 February 2018 says compliance with the involuntary resettlement safeguard "was deemed to be satisfactory during implementation". Neither counts anyone moved or records a payment shortfall. The counts are in the plan: the abbreviated resettlement plan of 26 April 2012 says "Au total, dix (10) biens ont ete affectes appartenant a six (6) PAP" and describes them as four individuals, a private school and Benin Telecom; the review turns the same figure into "ten properties involving six Project-Affected-People (PAP) and some businesses and institutions could be affected". ICIJ's 6 is that plan figure.

p095210-niger-agro-pastoral-export.drop_reason: Niger Agro-Pastoral Export and Market Development Project (PRODEX). Checked in the outcome document: the completion report of 24 April 2018 says at paragraph 54 that mitigation measures recommended by the subproject screening were implemented and evaluated afterwards, and that "Specific cases, such as the road sub-projects, required the preparation and implementation of brief resettlement action plans." It gives no count of people moved, no site and no payment shortfall. The one adverse finding is about data: monitoring of groundwater in the irrigation subproject zones "has not been systematic", which affected the quality of the data. The Evaluation Group's review of 18 July 2018 repeats that and adds nothing on resettlement. ICIJ gives 3.

p073629-cameroon-community-development-p.drop_reason: Cameroon Community Development Program Support Project (PNDP), first phase. Checked in the outcome document: the completion report of 25 May 2010 says at paragraph 49 that "Only two cases (out of more than 300 subprojects) of involuntary displacements were recorded during Project implementation. Adequate measures were taken to resettle the concerned parties back to their initial site." That is a count of cases, not of people or households, the subprojects are not named, and the report records the people as returned to where they started. ICIJ's 2 is this figure. The same paragraph says that for all the other subprojects built on private land a letter showing the land had been donated to the commune or community was attached to the financing request, and that communal authorities were advised to start registering the donated land; the report records no coercion and counts no donor. Paragraph 46 says eight safeguard policies were triggered and that action was taken on three of them. The Evaluation Group's review of 24 March 2011 adds nothing on either point. This is the closest call among the drops in this batch: a recorded involuntary displacement with no people-bearing count and no loss left standing.

p111338-lome-infrastructure-rehabilitati.drop_reason: Lome Infrastructure Rehabilitation and Maintenance Project, Togo. No outcome document exists on any route tried. Two routes failed: the Bank's document list query for this project number, which returns exactly one document, the resettlement policy framework of 1 April 2008; and a project list query for Togo, which returns 159 projects and no parent or sibling under which a completion report for this grant is filed. The Bank's own project record gives a grant of US$1,575,000 approved on 23 May 2008 with a closing date of 30 June 2010, and no commitment amount, status or lending instrument. ICIJ records no displacement estimate for it. The resettlement policy framework is a framework: it sets out who must be compensated and how the number of affected people is to be estimated, and records no works and no person affected.
